picked: PaddleOCR-VL 1.6, a vision-language document parser of about 0.9 billion parameters, bf16 precision, Apache-2.0
why: Digitises the scanned package under a license the operator holds outright, running as released with human reconciliation before any value enters the register

picked: CDEGS or COMSOL, industry-recognized validated electromagnetic and grounding software at the site tier
why: The governing clauses require validated software and score unsupported modelling lower, so the interference physics never leaves mandated tools

picked: One server-class host of the 48 GB PCIe inference GPU class inside the operator's estate
why: Holds the parser weights under 2 GB and leaves the balance of the card for concurrent solver runs and parser sessions

picked: Weights against usable memory first, solver memory with headroom second; context length never binds
why: The parser reads single scanned pages, so the kv cache ceiling is never the constraint the card is sized on

picked: Pipe-to-soil DC potential at corridor test points, in volts against the copper-copper sulfate electrode with the protective criterion at -0.85 V, plus four-pin soil resistivity by corridor section
why: The physical world is sensed by electrical measurement, not imaging: no camera duty exists anywhere in the scope

picked: A provenance-carrying validation register, marking every attribute measured, inherited, assumed or unknown
why: Data errors are the contractor's cost, so every correction has to be traceable and cost-defensible

picked: A re-runnable model handed over on the operator's own hardware, with no consultant-side copy surviving handover
why: The compiled records and software are the procuring agency's absolute property, and a federal public sector corporation sits under the national cloud-first policy

picked: One site-tier host on existing power and cooling inside the operator's facility
why: No field compute, no new network and no data crossing the boundary, so the stack runs where the data already sits
